key_insight: Heat losses to the channel walls strongly alter early premixed flame propagation, promoting tulip flame formation and later distortion in confined hydrogen-air channels.
engineering_relevance: For combustion safety and microchannel design, wall thermal management and geometry must be accounted for because they can change flame shape, speed, and stability.
method: Direct numerical simulation of the fully compressible reactive Navier–Stokes equations.
Stoichiometric hydrogen-air chemistry with detailed transport and kinetics.
Coupled gas-phase flame dynamics with conductive heat transfer through channel walls and external heat loss models.
evidence_signal: The simulations were compared against adiabatic-wall cases and reproduced the main experimentally observed features of flame evolution, including tulip and distorted tulip flames.
watch_item: Results depend on high-fidelity chemistry, transport, and wall heat-transfer modeling, so simplified boundary conditions may miss important flame-structure effects.
paper_title: The Effect of Heat Loss During the Early Stages of Flame Propagation and Tulip Flame Formation
